posts.text:
Is 2027 the year of agentic finance?

Base's Jesse Pollak says his AI agents now run his books, budget, and trades, and even find him yields he never had time to access

"They're getting big and growing. Still small in the grand scheme of overall payments volume, but we definitely are seeing growth on Base."

"All of these are going to be doing payments on behalf of people, and so I expect it to grow very quickly."

"I think 2026 is kind of the year where agentic payments emerge. My sense is that 2027 is going to be the year where agentic finance really emerges."

"We're seeing the early signs of this already. People using these agents to manage their whole financial life. And I've actually moved to doing this entirely."

"My agents are now doing all of my bookkeeping, all of my accounting, all of my budgeting. They're telling me about my investments. They're letting me trade on Coinbase."

"They're letting me do things in terms of accessing yield that I wasn't really able to do before, because I just didn't have the time."

Crypto is taking off. So why aren't bags pumping?

Base's Jesse Pollak says this is what mainstream adoption looks like, with less than 1% of the world's dollars and equities onchain

"There's almost like a weird feeling at times in crypto over the last year, where I think people feel almost a dissonance of like, oh my god, it's so clear that we're taking off from a product market fit and growth perspective, but maybe this isn't what we expected, and maybe it's not pumping our bags."

"The way I look at this is, this is what mainstream adoption looks and feels like."

"When you have a technology that is getting adopted by the biggest financial companies in the world because it offers faster, cheaper, better financial services, I think that's the vision that we've been building towards now for 13 years."

"Look at stablecoins or look at equities. We have less than 1% of the world's dollars, less than 1% of the world's equities moving on these new rails."

"Over the next 5 years, 10 years, it's going to be about going from less than 1% to 10% to 50% to 90%, and that is just a massive, massive pie."

The global copper market is extremely tight:

China's copper import premium over London Metal Exchange (LME) prices has surpassed $200 per ton, the largest premium on record.

The Yangshan premium, named after a Shanghai port that serves as a major hub for Chinese copper imports, has more than doubled over the last 3 months.

Since the beginning of 2026, this figure has surged +700%.

Furthermore, the premium of spot prices over three-month futures on the LME widened to $217 per ton, the largest since mid-August.

This has been driven by strong Chinese copper demand and domestic inventories falling below typical seasonal levels.

At the same time, expectations of potential US tariffs on refined copper have redirected hundreds of thousands of tons of copper to the US, leaving global inventories heavily concentrated in the country.

The physical copper supply squeeze is far from over.

Had 5 roommates in a 3 br apt.  Ate lousy food out of cans and ate  a ton of peanuts and shit food  at happy hour.  Had credit cards ripped up.  Etc.  

But I learned a ton.  Taught me what was right and wrong about running a business by watching my bosses and their bosses 

Yeah I know. It was much easier then, when inflation was 15 pct and national unemployment was 10 %.  I know I was fortunate when I finally got fired from the store, and had to start my own business with zero cash.   Bill collectors everywhere. 
Even luckier when I found my first customer so I could pay my bills

But I recognize it’s so much harder today.  

Which is why I respect the people who are willing to do what it takes to get started

Hey @grok 

Explain how the one-day Friday selloff in the tech sector ranked historically in tech selloffs in one-day moves based on total tech market cap loss and total capital lost by investors.

posts.name: Steve Burns
posts.text:
One of the most useful things to measure after earnings isn't the size of the gap.

Measure how much of that gap survives.
A stock that gaps 12% and keeps 11% has processed the new information very differently from one that gaps 12% and finishes up 2%.

The announcement creates the gap.
The price action afterward tells you what traders ultimately decided about the move.
